Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're getting close to contract signature and want to lock the operational intake before the legal/finance paperwork finishes. High level: HelixSphere needs a dedicated GPU pool for our inference workload (long seq chat + retrieval calls). Key asks:
- Target QPS for steady state: ~180 rps (token sizes vary).
- Peak burst tolerance: up to 450 rps for regional launches.
- Preferred region: us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 failover.
- Hard constraints: data must stay in customer VPC, and we need 1-week blackout window for cutover to validate telemetry.

Could you send us the intake template and a proposed cutover playbook with autoscale/burst policy recommendations? Also want to surface any network/peering requirements ahead of time.

Appreciate it — Alex

Alex / team — quick technical addendum:
- Network: We'll need outbound NAT for model pulls (if Helix wants to keep images in their registry), plus inbound rules from HelixSphere VPC to the Redwood dedicated VPC for health checks. Typical ports: 443 (HTTPS), 10250-10260 (internal perf traces), 9090 (metrics), 12345 (KV cache control; if you opt into our cache federation). We'll include a tidy port matrix in the Drive link.
- Autoscale policy: baseline min replicas for 200 rps; step-scaling triggers at 250/350/450 rps with a 30s cooldown. Burst buffer: maintain 1-2 warm GPUs per AZ (configurable) to absorb sudden spikes. If Helix uses token-level cost caps, we can route traffic to a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical routes.
- Observability gating for cutover: require 5m rolling latency median under target and no error rate >0.5% for 2 consecutive 30m windows during validation.

I'll attach network_diagram_v2.pdf and a short runbook snippet.

- Ben

Priya — good questions. Short answers and where to find the details:
- Cold-to-warm: with our pre-warm policy, cold-to-warm (one GPU spin-up) is ~120s in worst case; warm-to-ready for adding replicas behind traffic is ~20-40s depending on model size. That's why we recommend 1-2 warm GPUs per AZ in the burst buffer.
- Quantized fallback: typical latency reduction of 25-40% depending on model; small quality delta on short-answer prompts, larger on long-chain reasoning. We recommend running your evaluation prompts through our Optimize bench during the prep window; we'll surface a recommend threshold for automated fallback routing.

I've updated the intake template with these estimates and added an SLT column. Marissa — can you confirm we'll plan the cutover for the second week of January and own the customer communications for the blackout validation window? I'll set up the technical kickoff with Ben + Helix SREs for Thu at 14:00 PT.

Thanks,
